title: Bayesian model updating via streamlined Bayesian active learning cubature
abstractText: This paper proposes a novel Bayesian active learning method for Bayesian model updating, which is termed as "Streamlined Bayesian Active Learning Cubature" (SBALC). The core idea is to approximate the log-likelihood function using Gaussian process (GP) regression in a streamlined Bayesian active learning way. Rather than generating many samples from the posterior GP, we only use its mean and variance function to form the model evidence estimator, stopping criterion, and learning function. Specifically, the estimation of model evidence is first treated as a Bayesian cubature problem, with a GP prior assigned over the log-likelihood function. Second, a plug-in estimator for model evidence is proposed based on the posterior mean function of the GP. Third, an upper bound on the expected absolute error between the posterior model evidence and its plug-in estimator is derived. Building on this result, a novel stopping criterion and learning function are proposed using only the posterior mean and standard deviation functions of the GP. Finally, we can obtain the model evidence based on the posterior mean function of the log-likelihood function in conjunction with Monte Carlo simulation, as well as the samples for the posterior distribution of model parameters as a by-product. Four numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method compared to several existing approaches. The results show that the method can significantly reduce the number of model evaluations and the computational time without compromising accuracy.

title: Impacto del uso intensivo de herramientas digitales en la capacidad de concentración académica
abstractText: El presente estudio analizó el impacto del uso intensivo de herramientas digitales en la capacidad de concentración académica en estudiantes de educación superior. En un contexto de hiperconectividad global, caracterizado por la exposición constante a dispositivos móviles, redes sociales y plataformas digitales, emergen interrogantes sobre sus efectos en los procesos cognitivos implicados en el aprendizaje profundo. El objetivo general fue determinar la relación entre el tiempo de uso de herramientas digitales y los niveles de atención sostenida en estudiantes universitarios. La investigación adoptó un enfoque cuantitativo, de diseño no experimental y alcance correlacional. Se aplicó una encuesta estructurada con escala Likert a estudiantes universitarios, cuyos datos fueron procesados mediante el sistema estadístico SPSS, utilizando análisis descriptivos y coeficientes de correlación. Los resultados evidenciaron que el 65,63% de los estudiantes utiliza dispositivos digitales más de cinco horas diarias, mientras que el 59,38% reporta dificultades para mantener la concentración en actividades académicas prolongadas. Se identificó una correlación negativa moderada entre el uso intensivo de herramientas digitales y la atención sostenida. Se concluye que la exposición prolongada y no regulada a entornos digitales puede incidir en la fragmentación cognitiva, afectando los procesos de concentración académica. Se recomienda el diseño de estrategias pedagógicas orientadas al fortalecimiento de la autorregulación digital y la atención profunda en educación superior.

title: ORDINAL-EVIDENTIAL DYNAMIC HYPERGRAPH STATE-SPACE LEARNING FOR RELIABLE CHILD ENGAGEMENT RISK PREDICTION
abstractText: The recognition of children's engagement and behavioural risk is critical to building a trusted AI-based approach to education and mental health support. However, current work shows that common engagement-recognition methods lack modelling of complex facial–temporal interactions, do not capture the ordering of engagement states, are prone to class imbalance, and often yield overconfident predictions in ambiguous behavioural settings. This study introduces OE-DHSSNet and the ER-MOBH optimisation strategy for uncertainty-aware and explainable engagement assessment. A selective state-space temporal encoder models long-range behavioural dependencies at low computational cost, and the framework establishes dynamic hypergraph relationships among behaviour-related, facial, and motion cues. An ordinal-evidential prediction head jointly estimates engagement levels and predictive uncertainty, while ER-MOBH jointly optimises predictive performance, calibration, and inference latency under constraints. The framework is built around the DAiSEE dataset, which provides four-level engagement labels, and also includes an EmotiW-based branch for out-of-distribution reliability analysis. In an illustrative, simulation-based evaluation designed to exercise the intended experimental protocol, the optimised OE-DHSSNet configuration reached an accuracy of 95.81%, a macro-F1 score of 94.45%, and a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.947, with an expected calibration error of 0.023 and an expected latency of approximately 32.6 ms per video sample. Explainability analysis further indicated that, for the 'Very High' engagement category, the eye/upper-face contribution (44%) was higher than for the 'Very Low' engagement condition (19%), whereas the head-pose/motion contribution was lower for 'Very High' (14%) than for 'Very Low' (42%). Evidential uncertainty correspondingly grew from 0.06 to 0.24, the expected direction for increasingly ambiguous behaviour. The proposed framework can thus help future educational-monitoring and early behavioural-risk-support AI systems, which must be trustworthy, by offering a unified approach to ordinal engagement recognition, uncertainty quantification and calibration, multi-objective optimisation, and interpretable behavioural assessment.

title: Konsep Azwāj Dalam Al-Qur’an (Analisis Tafsir Muhammad Asad)
abstractText: Penelitian ini membahas konsep azwāj dalam Al-Qur’an melalui analisis terhadap karya tafsir Muhammad Asad, The Message of the Qur’an. Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh pentingnya merekonstruksi pemahaman tentang konsep pasangan dalam Al-Qur’an guna merespons berbagai kompleksitas dan disrupsi hubungan keluarga di era kontemporer. Dalam Al-Qur’an, konsep azwāj tidak hanya merujuk pada relasi biologis-pernikahan antara laki-laki dan perempuan, tetapi juga memuat prinsip kepasangan, keserasian, keseimbangan, serta kemitraan yang berdimensi moral dan spiritual. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis penafsiran Muhammad Asad mengenai azwāj serta merumuskan relevansi konseptual dan kontekstualnya bagi bangunan keluarga modern. Penelitian ini merupakan studi kepustakaan (library research) berbasis kualitatif dengan menggunakan metode tafsir tematik (mawḍū‘ī). Analisis difokuskan pada ayat-ayat utama tentang azwāj, seperti Surah Al-Baqarah ayat 25, Ar-Rum ayat 21, An-Nisa ayat 1 dan An-Nahl ayat 72, Ad-Dukhan ayat 54, Al-Mu’minun ayat 6 dan Ar-Rahman ayat 52 yang ditelaah melalui pendekatan hermeneutik-rasional Asad. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Asad memaknai azwāj secara holistik sebagai kemitraan eksistensial yang berlandaskan prinsip kesetaraan asal-usul, keselarasan peran, dan saling melengkapi (complementarity). Secara konseptual, penafsiran ini menawarkan artikulasi teoritis yang relevan bagi masyarakat kontemporer untuk membangun relasi keluarga berbasis penghormatan mutlak, kesetaraan emosional, dan tanggung jawab etik bersama, sekaligus mengoreksi pandangan hierarkis-patriarkal yang acapkali memicu konflik domestik.

Cross-cultural modeling of body satisfaction using social media selfies and self-descriptions
abstractText: Abstract Body satisfaction is a core component of psychological well-being and is closely intertwined with how individuals present themselves on social media. While prior research has examined body image through self-report measures or qualitative analyses of online content, it remains unclear whether body satisfaction is systematically associated with naturally occurring multimodal self-presentation behaviors, particularly across cultural contexts.In this study, we propose a cross-cultural multimodal mixed-methods framework to examine self-reported body satisfaction using social media selfies and self-descriptions. A sample of 240 participants from Western and East Asian cultural contexts provided self-reported body satisfaction measures alongside selected social media images and textual materials. Visual features were extracted using convolutional neural networks, while linguistic features were derived from multilingual transformer-based language models. These modalities were integrated through a late-fusion strategy to examine the extent to which multimodal self-presentational features were associated with self-reported body satisfaction.Results indicate that multimodal models outperform single-modality approaches in both regression and classification tasks. Moreover, feature importance and explainability analyses reveal culturally differentiated patterns of self-presentation: visual cues such as facial expression and body posture were more predictive in Western participants, whereas contextual and linguistic cues contributed more strongly among East Asian participants. Qualitative analyses of a purposively selected subset of misclassified and high-attention cases further illustrate cultural patterns in self-expression, modesty, and self-objectification strategies.Together, these findings suggest that body satisfaction is systematically associated with multimodal social media self-presentation and that cultural context plays an important role in shaping how such associations manifest online. This study illustrates the value of integrating computational modeling with qualitative interpretation to advance cross-cultural research on body image and digital mental health, while underscoring that predictive associations should not be interpreted as causal, clinical, or diagnostic evidence.

title: HONING PROCESS OPTIMIZATION IN ENGINE COMPONENT REMANUFACTURING: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF METHODS, PARAMETERS, FUNCTIONAL PERFORMANCE METRICS AND CAM INTEGRATION
abstractText: Honing is the most precise abrasive finishing process used to achieve the dimensional accuracy, surface integrity and functional cross-hatch surface texture of the internal cylindrical surfaces of an engine. In engine remanufacturing it has an extra weight as a worn cylinder bore or relining sleeve will require a cylinder bore that is both back to standard and capable of sealing pistons, lubricating the engine and maintaining good piston ring performance. The present systematic review, which follows the PRISMA 2020 reporting guideline, gathers and summarizes 39 studies related to honing optimisation of cylinder sleeves, liners and similar bores, as well as contextual studies on design of experiments (DOE), condition monitoring and Industry 4.0 in a developing-economy context. It reviews conventional, multi-stage plateau, slide, variable-kinematics and non-conventional (electrochemical and magnetorheological) honing as well as the main variables that can be controlled (abrasive grain size and density, honing pressure, rotational and reciprocating speed, stroke, cross-hatch angle, time and tool expansion), and the performance criteria used to evaluate them (roughness, material-ratio and areal parameters, cylindricity, material removal rate, tool wear, energy and productivity). The results demonstrate that the influences of the parameters are related to the honing stages, the abrasive system, the material of the workpiece, and the texture of the object to be honed; so honing should be considered as a multi-response problem. The resolution of conflicting optima is a common feature of the Taguchi, ANOVA, grey relational analysis, desirability and neuro-fuzzy models, which is evident across the authors' experience in DOE in milling, injection moulding, additive manufacturing and wood machining. The Rk-family and the ISO 25178-2 parameters are more suitable to describe the function of cylinder-liners than the Ra alone. The review highlights eight research gaps, such as core-condition-aware parameter selection, functional-metrology-based objectives, energy and carbon accounting, stone-wear evolution and skills and proposes a CAM-integrated, data-driven framework for repeatable remanufacturing.

Sepsis en 2026, partiendo de una respuesta de manejo inicial precoz hacia un sistema integral de atención en el Departamento de Emergencia
abstractText: La sepsis continúa siendo una de las principales emergencias médicas a nivel mundial y representa un desafío permanente para los servicios de emergencia y los sistemas de salud. Su atención ha evolucionado desde estrategias centradas principalmente en intervenciones durante las primeras horas hacia un modelo más individualizado e integrado a lo largo del continuo asistencial. Las recomendaciones de la Surviving Sepsis Campaign de 2026 consolidan esta transición al incorporar reconocimiento prehospitalario, estratificación temprana, uso responsable de antimicrobianos, reanimación guiada por la respuesta fisiológica, mejora de la calidad y continuidad posterior al episodio agudo. Para los sistemas de salud latinoamericanos, el reto no consiste únicamente en conocer estas recomendaciones, sino en traducirlas en procesos asistenciales reproducibles y adaptados a diferentes niveles de disponibilidad de recursos. La sepsis debe entenderse no solo como una emergencia tiempo-dependiente, sino también como un indicador de la capacidad del sistema para reconocer, responder, reevaluar y garantizar continuidad asistencial.

title: POCUS en el choque séptico: de herramienta complementaria a estándar de cuidado
abstractText: El choque séptico continúa asociándose a una elevada carga asistencial y a una incertidumbre diagnóstica considerable: los sistemas de alerta y predicción actuales, aun con buena discriminación estadística, muestran alta variabilidad institucional y bajo valor predictivo positivo . Paralelamente, un cuarto de siglo de ensayos de reanimación hemodinámica basados en objetivos fisiológicos fijos (presión venosa central, saturación venosa central de oxígeno, aclaramiento de lactato) no ha logrado traducirse de forma reproducible en mejores desenlaces centrados en el paciente. El Ultrasonido en el punto de atención (Point of Care Ultrasound POCUS) ofrece una vía alternativa: fenotipificación hemodinámica cambiante y repetible mediante protocolos como RUSH, VExUS y la evaluación combinada de elevación pasiva de piernas (PLR) con integral velocidad-tiempo del tracto de salida del ventrículo izquierdo (LVOT-VTI). La evidencia diagnóstica y fisiológica es consistente, y las guías Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026 ya recomiendan el uso de medidas dinámicas —entre ellas el POCUS — por encima del examen físico o las medidas estáticas aisladas. Sin embargo, los metaanálisis centrados en mortalidad muestran resultados heterogéneos y de certeza baja a moderada, y el uso real de POCUS en la práctica sigue siendo desigual y dependiente del operador. La evidencia actual no basta para declarar el POCUS un estándar universal de mortalidad, pero se puede reconocer que ha dejado de ser un complemento opcional. Proponemos que la vía intermedia y responsable es la estandarización: entrenamiento estructurado obligatorio y protocolos institucionales (RUSH/VExUS) como puente hacia un verdadero estándar de cuidado.

COMPARATIVE IN VITRO ANTIBACTERIAL ACTIVITY OF GARLIC ESSENTIAL OIL AND CINNAMON BARK EXTRACT AGAINST PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA
abstractText: The present study compared the antibacterial activity and mechanism of action of hydrodistilled essential oil of Allium sativum (garlic) versus 70% v/v ethanolic bark extract from Cinnamomum verum (cinnamon) against a multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain resistant to β lactams third generation cephalosporins, with intermediate susceptibility to imipenem and ciprofloxacin. Inhibition was observed to be dose dependent, as seen in the agar diffusion assays. At 100 mg/mL, garlic essential oil produced a zone of clearance of 32 mm, about 4 mm wider than the 28 mm at the lower concentration (25 mg/mL). The effect of the cinnamon extract (average zones of inhibition of 18 and 28 mm at 25 and 100 mg/mL, respectively) was moderate. Garlic oil was also confirmed to be more potent compared to cinnamon extract at a MIC of 0.50 mg/mL versus 1.00 mg/mL, respectively, by broth microdilution. Profiling of garlic oil by high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) indicated the presence of allicin and other related organosulfur derivatives as major components, while cinnamon extract was mostly active due to trans cinnamaldehyde. Mechanistically, the bactericidal properties of garlic oil have been attributed to thiol disulfide exchange reactions between allicin and essential sulfhydryl (–SH) groups on bacterial enzymes, which ultimately result in enzyme inactivation, redox imbalance, and rapid cell death. Conversely, trans cinnamaldehyde induces a destabilization of the bacterial inner membrane through direct intercalation, dissipates the proton motive force, and eliminates internal ATP stores while inhibiting the cell division protein FtsZ. The marked susceptibility of this P. aeruginosa to these botanical preparations suggests potential activity against a resistant phenotype, a conventional possible antibacterial mechanism of β-lactamase and efflux mediated resistance. In particular, garlic essential oil stands out as a promising scaffold for therapeutic development against hard-to-treat P. aeruginosa infections.

Life‑cycle analysis of bio‑based phase change materials in recycled‑aggregate mortars: sourcing sensitivity and trade‑offs
abstractText: Abstract The decarbonization of construction materials requires circular design strategies supported by life‑cycle thinking. This study quantifies the cradle‑to‑gate (A1–A3) environmental impacts of three mortar formulations: (i) a Reference mortar, (ii) a mortar incorporating recycled wood aggregates, and (iii) a hybrid mortar in which recycled wood aggregates are impregnated with a bio‑based phase change material to provide latent‑heat storage functionality. A Life Cycle Assessment compliant with ISO 14044 and EN 15804 was implemented in SimaPro using Ecoinvent, focusing on fossil embodied greenhouse-gas emissions (IPCC GWP100a) and total Cumulative Energy Demand (CED). For a performance-related material-scale comparison, results were additionally normalized by volumetric thermal capacity. Because a dedicated inventory for the commercial bio‑based phase change material (PureTemp 25) is not publicly available, a scenario‑based sensitivity analysis was performed using four alternative feedstock proxies (coconut, palm, palm kernel, and Reference mortar has the lowest GWP soybean). Each feedstock was modeled separately, and the unweighted arithmetic mean of the four scenario results was used as a representative central estimate; this value does not represent a physical or equal-proportion mixture of oils. On this basis, replacing conventional constituents with recycled alternatives reduced impacts substantially, reaching up to 82% lower IPCC GWP and 36% lower CED for the hybrid mortar compared with the conventional reference. Feedstock choice strongly influenced trade‑offs, particularly land use and water consumption, highlighting the importance of responsible sourcing for bio‑based components. The results provide decision‑support evidence for the sustainable design of circular, functionality‑enhanced building materials.

title: Analisis Nilai Tambah dan Kelayakan Produksi Pengolahan Latek Scrap Menjadi Crumb Rubber Pada CV. Tunas Bangsa OKU Timur
abstractText: Keterbatasan optimalisasi nilai tambah pada sisa hasil panen karet berupa lateks scrap di Kabupaten OKU Timur menjadi permasalahan ekonomi utama bagi petani lokal karena sering dianggap sebagai limbah bernilai rendah. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis besarnya nilai tambah yang dihasilkan dari pengolahan lateks scrap menjadi crumb rubber spesifikasi Standard Indonesian Rubber 20 serta menguji tingkat kelayakan finansial usahanya pada CV. Tunas Bangsa. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah studi kasus dengan pendekatan deskriptif kuantitatif. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui observasi lapangan, wawancara terstruktur, dan studi dokumentasi operasional perusahaan. Data dianalisis menggunakan metode Hayami untuk menghitung nilai tambah serta analisis kriteria investasi finansial yang mencakup Net Present Value, Internal Rate of Return, dan Net Benefit-Cost Ratio. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa proses pengolahan lateks scrap menjadi crumb rubber menghasilkan nilai tambah positif sebesar Rp5.595 per kilogram bahan baku dengan rasio nilai tambah sebesar 48,96 persen yang tergolong dalam kategori sedang. Evaluasi kelayakan finansial menunjukkan nilai Net Present Value sebesar Rp2.776.859.537,21, Internal Rate of Return sebesar 70,56 persen, dan Net Benefit-Cost Ratio sebesar 5,88. Berdasarkan hasil analisis tersebut, dapat disimpulkan bahwa pengolahan lateks scrap menjadi crumb rubber di CV. Tunas Bangsa mampu memberikan nilai tambah ekonomi yang menguntungkan serta sangat layak secara finansial untuk dikembangkan lebih lanjut karena memiliki daya tahan bisnis dan efisiensi investasi yang tinggi.

title: Landscape genomics on Acrocomia aculeata trees aiming breeding selection
abstractText: Abstract Acrocomia aculeata is a promising oil-producing palm whose breeding is constrained by its long juvenile period, high costs of phenotypic evaluations, and limited genomic resources. Here, we present an integrative framework combining landscape genomics and genomic selection to support breeding strategies in A . aculeata . Spatial and genomic information from 167 individuals, distributed across four provenances, was analyzed using three SNP-calling strategies: a de novo pipeline, the Elaeis guineensis reference genome, the A. aculeata transcriptome; and a combined SNP dataset. Population structure and genetic diversity were evaluated across provenances. Genomic selection models were developed for pulp dry mass (PDM), kernel dry mass (KDM), and oil content (OC) using leave-one-out and provenance-based validation. Population analyses revealed low genetic differentiation among provenances (F ST = 0.001–0.003), indicating that the trees constitute a single population. Genomic prediction achieved predictive abilities of up to 0.35 for PDM, 0.43 for KDM, and 0.50 for OC with the oil palm genome and combined SNP datasets showing the most consistent predictive performance. Incorporating a spatial kernel showed that environmental effects accounted for up to 69.32% of the phenotypic variance in OC. Spatial genomic prediction identified superior genotypes for simultaneous improvement of the traits , which were distributed throughout the landscape rather than concentrated within specific provenances. Overall, our results suggest that seed collection based on individually superior trees may be more effective than collection based solely on geographic provenance and highlight the potential of integrating genomic prediction to exploit natural genetic diversity and accelerating the breeding of native species.

Pendekatan Diagnosis Lahan Berbasis Sumber Daya Lokal untuk Mendukung Pemberdayaan Kelompok Tani Melalui Penyusunan Rekomendasi Pengelolaan Lahan
abstractText: Rekomendasi pengelolaan lahan bagi kelompok tani masih sering disusun secara umum tanpa mempertimbangkan kondisi biofisik spesifik lokasi dan ketersediaan sumber daya lokal, sehingga kesesuaiannya dapat berbeda antarlokasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis kondisi biofisik dan faktor pembatas, mengidentifikasi potensi sumber daya lokal, menyusun rekomendasi pengelolaan spesifik lokasi, serta merumuskan KERDILA (Kerangka Diagnosis Lahan dan Rekomendasi Pengelolaan) sebagai kerangka pendukung keputusan. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif dengan desain studi multi-lokasi pada empat kawasan pertanian perkotaan binaan program tanggung jawab sosial dan lingkungan PT Pertamina Patra Niaga Aviation Fuel Terminal Sepinggan di Kota Balikpapan. Data diperoleh melalui pemeriksaan lapangan menggunakan soil analyzer tester, observasi kondisi tanah, air, tanaman, dan sistem budidaya, dokumentasi, dokumen program, serta materi pendampingan teknis, kemudian dianalisis melalui reduksi, kategorisasi, perbandingan antarlokasi, dan matching analysis. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa keempat lokasi memiliki perbedaan kemasaman tanah, tingkat kesuburan, kelembapan tanah, kualitas air, sistem budidaya, dan sumber daya lokal yang tersedia, sehingga setiap lokasi memerlukan paket rekomendasi yang berbeda. title: STRENGTH OF MOTIVATION FOR MEDICAL SCHOOL-REVISED IN A SAMPLE OF IRAQI MEDICAL STUDENTS: SCORE PATTERNS AND PSYCHOMETRIC EVALUATION
abstractText: Objectives: Motivation is widely regarded as a critical determinant of learning outcomes, academic achievement, and overall well-being within the domain of medical education. Nevertheless, empirical investigations addressing this construct within the Iraqi context remain scarce, so this study design for mapping motivation patterns and evaluating the psychometric performance of the SMMS-R in a sample of Iraqi medical students. Methods: This cross-sectional study aimed to determine the patterns of motivation and to evaluate the psychometric properties of the Strength of Motivation for Medical School-Revised (SMMS-R) questionnaire among 384 medical students of all six years of study at Hammurabi College of Medicine, University of Babylon. This was achieved by using scale of 15 items which were organized into 3 subscales each with 5 subitems, these conducted to the students by online survey by English & Arabic. & statistical analysis of the responses were achieved through SPSS v 31. Results: Results of an anonymous online poll revealed that most students expressed moderate motivation levels (62.0%), followed by strong motivation (24.5%) and 13.5% with poor motivation. The highest scores were obtained on the Readiness to Start subscale (3.82±0.91), followed by the Persistence (3.60±0.61) and Willingness to Sacrifice (3.52±0.76) subscales. Regarding the psychometric qualities, the overall 15-item SMMS-R demonstrated excellent total internal consistency (α=0.862) and internal consistency at the subscale level was assessed as satisfactory to good (α=0.680–0.829). Motivational strength was significantly different by gender (t=−2.12, p=0.036) with female students scoring slightly higher than male students and by academic stage (F=2.50, p=0.030). However, the practical significance of both effects appeared to be modest. Conclusion: Taken together, these results support the SMMS-R as a reliable and psychometrically robust instrument for use within Iraqi medical education. Also, the findings suggest that although students enter training with a strong sense of commitment, sustained socioeconomic and curricular pressures likely contribute to shaping their generally moderate motivation levels over time.

title: Observing the observers of projects: reconceptualizing the PMO through a von Foersterian second-order cybernetics lens
abstractText: Purpose This conceptual study examines how an AI-enabled Project Management Office (A-PMO) can be understood as a second-order observing system rather than merely as an instrument that observes and controls projects. Drawing primarily on Heinz von Foerster and positioning his work in relation to management cybernetics, conversation theory, self-referential social systems and ethico-onto-epistemology, the research asks how a PMO can observe the distinctions through which human and algorithmic observers construct project-governance reality. Design/methodology/approach The research is presented as a reflexive theoretical essay rather than as an empirical study or a formal problematization analysis. Its mode of inquiry consists of: (1) reconstructing four von Foersterian distinctions; (2) re-entering those distinctions into the manuscript's own observer position; (3) contrasting them with established and critical PMO scholarship; and (4) deriving design propositions, observable indicators and possible empirical tests for an A-PMO. Findings The study develops four connected principles: non-trivial governance, eigenvalue-based recursive stability, protection of undecidable governance questions from algorithmic foreclosure and explicit observer inclusion. The five-layer A-PMO framework provides an organizational configuration through which these principles are translated into PMO practices, including decision rights logs, risk classifications, protection of minority viewpoints, accountability records, recurring service reviews and second-order audits. The central argument is that the A-PMO's task is not to eliminate governance uncertainty, but to preserve the conditions under which human decisions can still be meaningfully and accountably evaluated. Originality/value The study contributes a second-order theoretical account of the A-PMO: it reconceptualizes algorithmic project governance itself as a form of observation, thereby extending existing critical, sociotechnical and governance perspectives on PMOs with an epistemological layer that these perspectives do not yet supply.

Analytics and AI in Management
abstractText: The modern business world is changing rapidly with the increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) and predictive analytics. Earlier, businesses depended mainly on past data to understand what had already happened. Today, AI and analytics help organizations predict future situations and make better decisions based on available data. This change has given rise to the idea of “augmented intelligence”, in which AI works together with people to support their decisions instead of replacing them. This paper studies how the use of AI and predictive analytics is affecting businesses and the way managers make decisions. It focuses on the use of AI in daily work, the automation of routine tasks, access to analytical tools and the changing role of human judgment in decision-making. A survey of 35 management professionals (N = 35) was conducted to understand their practical experience of AI and analytics in the workplace. The results show that AI is already being used in many professional roles: about 88.6% of respondents said that their work involves both AI and analytics, and 82.9% said that AI has significantly reduced their workload.

THE TRANSFORMATION OF RAPID PROTOTYPING IN INDUSTRY 4.0: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF CLOUD-BASED ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING
abstractText: Industry 4.0 changes the dynamics of how additive manufacturing (AM) is used for product development and rapid prototyping. Cloud computing, Internet of Things (IoT), cyber physical systems (CPS), artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) and digital twins are increasingly becoming part of AM, providing enhanced connectivity, flexibility and access to manufacturing resources. However, the more technologies emerge and the greater the number of benefits that are touted, the more difficult it is to assess the extent to which cloud-based additive manufacturing (CBAM) has transformed rapid prototyping—let alone why its popularization remains stymied. This systematic review outlines the changes to rapid prototyping in the context of Industry 4.0 using CBAM. The literature published from 2016 to 2026 was retrieved from Google Scholar, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore and Emerald and screened according to the included and excluded criteria pre-designed, and reported using PRISMA 2020. The review categorises the enabling technologies based on function, data flow, consolidates the reported applications and benefits of the technologies, and identifies technical, operational, economic and organisational barriers to their adoption, specifically considering the needs of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and developing economies including Zimbabwe. The results demonstrate the potential of CBAM to provide access to manufacturing resources at distance, collaborative and iterative design, distributed manufacturing and stronger integration of digital and physical manufacturing systems. There are still major shortcomings, however, in cybersecurity, interoperability, data handling, network reliability, quality consistency and interoperability with heterogeneous systems. The evidence of technical feasibility is much greater than the evidence of long-term economic gains, industrial scalability and implementation in reality. The review thus suggests more rigorous industrial validation, shared interoperability and security rules, process-parameter knowledge-bases that can be reused and paths towards implementation that are low-cost and incremental for resource-poor manufacturers.

title: Trade-off between flux efficiency and metabolic control shapes enzyme allocation
abstractText: Abstract Efficient use of limited cellular resources is fundamental to metabolism. Although flux optimization is widely recognized as a central objective of metabolic networks, how flux efficiency influences the allocation of the metabolic proteome remains unclear and lacks direct validation. Here, we derive a simple analytical relationship linking the equilibrium constant (K) and the catalytic-abundance quotient (CAQ) of reactions within a pathway that defines the condition for maximal efficiency. By integrating reaction thermodynamics, enzyme kinetics, transcriptomic, and proteomic data, we compared enzyme allocation in glycolysis and the TCA cycle with this K-CAQ relationship across evolutionarily distant species, and showed that deviation from it can be explained by a trade-off between maximizing flux efficiency and concentrating flux control. Moreover, the drive to optimize glycolytic efficiency is strengthened under oncogenic signaling and a limited cellular budget for glycolytic enzymes. These findings establish a principle of Pareto optimality governing enzyme allocation in metabolic pathways and reveal key determinants of efficiency optimality in glycolysis.

Underground Coal Mine Fires in Dhanbad, Jharkhand: A Need for Comprehensive State Legislation to Protect the Right to Life and Environment
abstractText: The underground coal mine fires in the Jharia Coalfield of Dhanbad, Jharkhand, constitute one of India’s longest-running environmental and humanitarian crises. Burning continuously for over a century, these fires have caused extensive environmental degradation, air pollution, land subsidence, destruction of valuable coal reserves, and widespread displacement of local communities. Continuous exposure to toxic gases and particulate matter has resulted in serious public health concerns, including respiratory diseases, cardiovascular disorders, and other chronic illnesses, thereby threatening the fundamental right to life and a healthy environment guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India. Although several central enactments, including the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981, the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and the Mines Act, 1952, provide a general framework for environmental protection and mining regulation, they do not adequately address the unique challenges posed by underground coal mine fires. This article critically examines the constitutional and statutory obligations of the Union and the State Governments in preventing mine fires, protecting public health, ensuring environmental restoration, and rehabilitating affected communities. It argues that the absence of a comprehensive state-specific legal framework has contributed to fragmented governance and ineffective implementation of existing policies. The article proposes the enactment of a dedicated Jharkhand Underground Coal Mine Fire Prevention, Rehabilitation and Environmental Protection Act, establishing an independent statutory authority for fire prevention, environmental monitoring, scientific risk assessment, rehabilitation, compensation, and inter-agency coordination. Adopting a doctrinal research methodology based on constitutional provisions, statutory analysis, judicial precedents, government reports, and secondary literature, the article concludes that comprehensive state legislation is essential to uphold environmental justice, strengthen environmental governance, protect public health, ensure accountable rehabilitation, and secure the rights of present and future generations.

title: The circular economy, explained by AI
abstractText: Abstract Research on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the circular economy (CE) has largely examined how AI can improve circular operations. Much less attention has been paid to AI tools widely used to understand and reason about the CE, particularly large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT. Researchers, practitioners, students, and decision-makers use these tools to seek explanations and support reasoning about circularity. This paper examines what is at stake when LLM-generated accounts enter CE inquiry. As a conceptual contribution, it develops a framework for analysing how AI-supported CE knowledge is formed, how it may influence action, and what ethical implications follow. The Content dimension concerns the construction and credibility of CE knowledge, focusing on pattern-based generation, opaque and heterogeneous sources, and fragmentation within CE scholarship. The Transformative dimension considers how such knowledge may influence innovation and entrepreneurship, including whether familiar, optimisation-oriented approaches overshadow systemic alternatives. The Moral dimension addresses the risks of relying on LLM outputs, including operational indifference to truth, AI assertiveness, the absence of moral agency, and the need for human judgement and accountability. The paper argues that LLMs can widen access to CE knowledge and support inquiry, but cannot independently determine which interpretations are better supported, exercise the judgement required to challenge linear assumptions, or decide how environmental, social, and economic values should be balanced. It identifies governance priorities concerning transparency, expert scrutiny, human agency, and epistemic humility. The framework can also guide future empirical research on how LLM-generated accounts vary across models, prompts, languages, and user contexts.

title: Socio-Familial Factors and Amorous Affairs Tendencies among Married Secondary School Teachers in Akwa Ibom North-West Senatorial District, Nigeria
abstractText: This study investigated the relationship between socio-familial factors and amorous affairs tendencies among secondary school teachers in the Akwa Ibom North-West Senatorial District. The research was guided by three objectives and their corresponding research questions and hypotheses. A correlational research design was adopted for this study. The target population comprised 7,846 teachers from all public secondary schools in the Akwa Ibom North-West Senatorial District. A sample of 364 teachers was selected for the study using the multistage sampling technique. Two researcher-developed instruments entitled “Socio-Familial Factors Questionnaire (SFFQ)” and “Amorous Affairs Tendencies Questionnaire (AATQ)” were used for data collection. The instruments were face-validated by three experts in the Faculty of Education, two from the Department of Human Kinetics and Health Education, and one from the Department of Psychological Foundations of Education, University of Uyo. The reliability of the instruments was analysed using the Cronbach Alpha Statistical tool, which yielded reliability coefficients of 0.76 and 0.82. Data collected were analysed using Pearson Product Moment Correlation (PPMC) statistics to answer research questions and to test null hypotheses at the .05 level of significance. The findings of the study revealed that cultural norms, peer influence, family expectations have significant relationships with amorous affairs tendencies among secondary school teachers in the Akwa Ibom North-West Senatorial District. Based on the findings, it concluded that socio-familial factors are significantly related to amorous affairs tendencies among secondary school teachers in Akwa Ibom North-West. It was recommended among others that community health workers should develop awareness programmes that address cultural norms related to morality and fidelity, promoting values that discourage amorous affairs among teachers and members of the community.

title: Clinical management of metachromatic leukodystrophy cases identified in the German and Austrian Newborn screening pilots
abstractText: Abstract Background Metachromatic leukodystrophy (MLD) is a rapidly progressive leukodystrophy that leads to severe disability and early death if untreated. Autologous hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell gene therapy (HSPC-GT, atidarsagene autotemcel, arsa-cel) for early onset subtypes and allogenic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) for late onset disease substantially alters disease progression for early onset disease when administered before symptom onset, creating a strong rationale for newborn screening (NBS). At the same time, NBS technique for MLD in dried blood spots has recently been demonstrated to be robust and highly accurate. The aim was to give real-world results from the world’s first NBS pilots for clinical management and treatment of identified children. Methods Between September 2021 and July 2025, 359,282 newborns underwent NBS for MLD in two different laboratories in Germany and Austria using a three-tier algorithm integrating sulfatide quantification, arylsulfatase A (ARSA) activity measurement, and ARSA sequencing. Screen-positive infants underwent a predefined care pathway including standardized confirmatory diagnostics, genotype-based and biochemical prediction of disease onset, clinical assessment and management guiding early treatment and surveillance at the qualified treatment center (QTC) in Tübingen. Results Nine newborns screened positive and all were confirmed to have MLD (detection rate approximately 1 per 40,000). Based on genotype and leukocyte ARSA enzyme activity, disease onset prediction was possible in all of them. Seven infants were classified as having pre-symptomatic early-onset MLD and were referred for HSPC-GT. All treated infants showed preserved neurological function up to 30 months after treatment (median 18.5 months). Two infants predicted to develop late-onset MLD entered structured surveillance for treatment with HSCT and have remained clinically asymptomatic for CNS signs of disease. No false-positive or known false-negative results were observed. Conclusion These results from our pilot programs demonstrate that NBS enables reliable early identification of MLD and support streamlined care pathways leading to timely intervention. Importantly, this study provides real-world evidence illustrating that NBS for MLD can enable timely, pre-symptomatic treatment and structured surveillance within standard national healthcare systems. These findings further substantiate the value of NBS for MLD at a critical moment as several countries consider national implementation of MLD screening.

title: A CCL21 gene-modified dendritic cell vaccine combined with pembrolizumab in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: a phase I trial
abstractText: Abstract Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed treatment for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but resistance to these therapies is common. We report here results from a phase I trial combining intratumoral injection of a CCL21-expressing dendritic cell (CCL21-DC) vaccine with pembrolizumab in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03546361). The primary objectives were to determine the maximum administered dose (MAD) in the dose escalation phase and the objective response rate (ORR) in the dose expansion. Eleven patients were enrolled in the dose escalation cohort, and 12 patients were treated in the dose expansion cohort at the MAD of 3 ×10 7 cells/injection. The trial did not meet its primary endpoint for ORR as no objective responses were observed, though 36.8% of patients achieved a best response of stable disease. The combination therapy was well tolerated. Post-hoc analyses of longitudinal biopsies revealed that the therapy increased tumor infiltration by CD4+ T cells and novel T cell clones. Disease stability was associated with increased T cell receptor diversity and greater expansion of novel clones following therapy. However, many novel clones failed to persist over time, and immunosuppressive myeloid signaling signatures were identified across time points. Our findings overall demonstrated that CCL21-DC vaccination combined with pembrolizumab can promote T cell infiltration, but this did not translate into meaningful clinical efficacy, potentially due to limited tumor specificity of the T cell response and an inability to fully reprogram the tumor microenvironment.

abstractText: Abstract This study investigates the effect of oxidation temperature on the structural, electronic, and electrochemical properties of graphene oxide (GO) synthesized at 75, 95, and 115 °C. Increasing the oxidation temperature resulted in a reduction in crystallite size from 9.95 ± 1.24 to 8.05 ± 0.49 nm and a decrease in the interlayer spacing, accompanied by partial reorganization of the sp² carbon domains. The electrical properties were significantly improved, with enhanced carrier transport at higher oxidation temperatures. The optical band gap decreased from 4.11 to 3.69 eV, while the Urbach energy increased from 285 to 625 meV, indicating enhanced energetic disorder and band-tail formation. Electrochemical analysis revealed improved charge-transfer kinetics, with the charge-transfer resistance decreasing from 911 to 598 Ω and the relaxation time decreasing from 0.842 to 0.671 ms. The electrochemical response also showed a predominantly diffusion-controlled charge-storage contribution, while the apparent diffusion coefficient decreased from 2.094 × 10⁻⁷ to 5.792 × 10⁻⁸ cm²/s with increasing oxidation temperature. In contrast, the specific capacitance decreased from 668 to 328 F/g, which is attributed to the reduction of oxygen-containing redox-active sites and restricted ion accessibility. Despite the reduced capacitive performance, the capacitance retention improved from 84.25% to 95.84% after 6000 cycles. Overall, increasing oxidation temperature promotes electronic transport and electrochemical kinetics while reducing redox-based charge-storage capacity, demonstrating a clear trade-off between electronic conductivity, ion-transport behavior, and capacitive performance.

abstractText: Como disciplina científica, a economia interpreta e analisa fenômenos socioeconômicos. Para tal, as premissas ontológicas são fundamentais, pois permitem uma compreensão abrangente da natureza inerentemente dinâmica da realidade social. O pensamento de Thorstein Veblen, fundamentado nesses pressupostos, oferece uma base teórica para entender a realidade socioeconômica por meio da interação, interdependência e evolução contínua entre indivíduos e instituições, mediadas por hábitos de pensamento e comportamento. Este estudo sistematiza e explora tais pressupostos presentes no pensamento de Veblen, que possibilitam a análise de mudanças estruturais e comportamentais em termos de processos cumulativos, além de orientar a implementação de políticas voltadas ao desenvolvimento social.

title: Kesadaran Perempuan Kota Solok terhadap Fenomena Kekerasan dalam Rumah Tangga
abstractText: Domestic violence (KDRT) remains a problem affecting women, while awareness of how to recognize, understand, and respond to it has not yet fully developed. In Solok City, the view that domestic violence is a private matter also influences women’s courage to report violence and seek protection. This study aims to describe women’s awareness of the phenomenon of domestic violence in Solok City. The study employed a qualitative descriptive approach involving 46 purposively selected informants, comprising 38 married women, 2 informants from Dinas Pemberdayaan Perempuan dan Perlindungan Anak (DPPPA) in Solok City, and 6 members of the Solok City community. Data were collected through semistructured interviews and documentation, and then analyzed through the stages of data collection, reduction, and display, as well as conclusion drawing and verification. The analysis used the Social Identity Model of Collective Action (SIMCA) framework, encompassing social identity, perceived injustice, and group efficacy. The results showed that women’s awareness of domestic violence was beginning to develop, particularly in recognizing physical violence, verbal violence, and economic neglect and understanding the existence of reporting and protection services. However, this awareness remained insufficiently developed because domestic violence still tended to be understood as a personal matter and some forms of violence continued to be normalized. Trust in institutions, economic dependence, concerns about the consequences of reporting, and limited social support also influenced women’s courage in responding to domestic violence. These findings clarify the gap between recognizing violence and having the courage to respond to it, and indicate the relationship between women’s awareness and social, economic, and institutional conditions in the context of domestic violence in Solok City.

title: Underrated deep-water scleractinian species: an ecological study along the Italian coasts (Mediterranean Sea)
abstractText: Abstract Scleractinians are key components of Mediterranean mesophotic and bathyal benthic ecosystems, comprising 30 species known to occur below 40 m. A large ROV dataset, including 625 dives, each corresponding to a distinct geographical site, conducted between 40 and 1825 m across the Italian seas, was used to assess the diversity of this taxon, focusing on the distribution, habitat preferences, and population density of four Data Deficient, yet well-represented species: solitary Caryophyllia cyathus , Paracyathus pulchellus , and Javania cailleti , and colonial Thalamophyllia gasti . The study recorded 18 scleractinian species (representing 60% of the known deep ones) and analysed almost 2600 records of the four target species. Caryophyllia cyathus , Paracyathus pulchellus, and Thalamophyllia gasti were the most common, occurring between 80 and 150 m on inclined outcropping rocks encrusted with coralline algae along the continental platform, with major hotspots in the Tyrrhenian Sea and average densities ranging between 2.4 and 36 individuals or colonies m −2 . Thalamophyllia gasti was observed for the first time in a cave habitat in Southwest Sardinia, forming large colonies. Javania cailleti was recorded at only 4% of the investigated sites, mainly along the Northeast Sardinian canyons, Corse Channel, Dohrn Canyon, and on seamounts between 400 and 550 m. This species, thriving on Fe–Mn-rich rocks, thanatocoenoses, and coral frameworks, tolerated high levels of silting and occasionally formed dense populations, averaging 12 individuals m −2 . This study expands biogeographic and ecological knowledge of these four species, highlighting their environmental preferences and distribution hotspots and confirming their significant yet underappreciated role in benthic communities in the Mediterranean mesophotic and bathyal zones.

TIME–FREQUENCY CHARACTERIZATION AND SEVERITY SCREENING OF COUPLED HEAVE–PITCH MOTIONS OF AN S-175 CONTAINER SHIP
abstractText: This study characterizes coupled rigid-body heave and pitch motions of the S-175 U-Waters containership under irregular head-sea conditions and develops a non-modal severity measure for structural screening. A three-dimensional linear potential-flow model in ANSYS AQWA was used to simulate a long-crested JONSWAP sea state with Hs=1.2 m, peak frequency fp=0.23Hz, head waves, and a vessel speed of 12.5 knots over a 300 s record. Response statistics, moving RMS, continuous wavelet analysis, cross-correlation, and a normalized coupled-response severity index were applied. Heave varied from −0.01102 to 0.01230 m with an RMS of 0.00826 m, while pitch varied from −0.01349° to 0.01612° with an RMS of 0.01055°. Dominant response bands were approximately 0.08–0.11 Hz for heave and 0.10–0.13 Hz for pitch. The maximum heave–pitch cross-correlation was approximately 0.82 at a lag close to zero, indicating strong temporal coupling. The normalized severity index reached 1.00, with a mean of approximately 0.63; severity exceeded 0.50 for approximately 60% of the record and 0.75 for approximately 25%. The identified response bands encompass the rigid-body characteristic frequencies of 0.0866, 0.1111, and 0.1221 Hz, which are used only as independent reference markers. The results provide a practical basis for identifying elevated rigid-body response conditions for subsequent structural screening.

Multivalent antiviral conjugates enhance activity against Influenza via cross-linking viruses
abstractText: Abstract Long-acting drug–Fc conjugate (CD388) has emerged as a new class of antivirals against influenza A and B, yet the mechanisms governing how Fc conjugation reshapes small-molecule function remain undefined. Here we establish a programmable multivalent antiviral conjugates (AVCs) platform by click chemistry that enables flexible combination of valencies and conjugated drugs, allowing systematic interrogation of valency-dependent antiviral mechanisms. Using zanamivir as a model, mono-, di-, and trivalent zanamivir are conjugated with Fc, with trivalent zanamivir-Fc conjugates (AVC-Z3) exhibiting higher activity than lower-valent AVCs. AVC-Z3 induces inter-virion aggregation, thereby coupling blockade of viral entry with restriction of viral release. This cross-linking–mediated dual-stage inhibition represents a mechanistic shift from neuraminidase suppression to physical viral immobilization. Furthermore, trivalent peramivir-Fc conjugate (AVC-P3) is synthesised and exhibits stronger antiviral activity than AVC-Z3 in vitro, with much longer half-life in vivo than AVC-Z3, and CD388 with YTE mutation. The in vivo antivirus efficacy of AVC-P3 surpasses other AVCs, baloxavir, and CD388 in H1N1-, H3N2-, H5N1-, and influenza B-infection mice models. Together, our findings define ligand valency as a determinant of antiviral mechanism.

title: La hora dorada: La carrera contra la sepsis
abstractText: Existe una idea clara que debemos enlazar con la idea de sepsis, que, durante todos estos años de investigación, la evolución de la sepsis no consiste en redefinirla, sino consiste en comprender que el tiempo es el recurso terapéutico mas valioso que tenemos. En medicina de emergencias, el tiempo es el peor enemigo; muchas decisiones clínicas deben ser tomadas con poca información y en cuestión de minutos. Esta realidad es aún más clara cuando hablamos de sepsis. Se ha impulsado por años la definición de “la hora de oro”, con la finalidad de entender que el tiempo es un determinante del pronostico del paciente; y que el concepto de limitarnos podría ocasionar una venda en nuestros ojos. El paciente con sepsis es completamente dinámico, y cada minuto de retraso es una oportunidad perdida para modificar el desenlace del paciente; siendo el tiempo no solo una variable clínica, sino parte del tratamiento.

title: Sepsis
abstractText: El tercer volumen de la revista Emergencia, dedicado a la sepsis, nace con el propósito de acercar el conocimiento científico a una realidad que vivimos todos los días en los servicios de emergencia: tomar decisiones importantes en muy poco tiempo. Frente a la sepsis, reconocer temprano al paciente, iniciar el tratamiento adecuado y trabajar de manera coordinada puede cambiar por completo su evolución. Esta edición reúne evidencia actual y experiencia clínica sobre reconocimiento precoz, reanimación, terapia antimicrobiana y soporte hemodinámico, pero también invita a mirar más allá de protocolos y algoritmos. Nuestro verdadero desafío sigue siendo lograr que la evidencia llegue oportunamente a la cabecera del paciente y se transforme en decisiones seguras y aplicables a nuestra realidad. Porque detrás de cada diagnóstico de sepsis existe una persona, una familia y un equipo de salud enfrentando momentos decisivos. Este volumen reafirma así nuestro compromiso con una Medicina de Emergencias crítica, actualizada y profundamente humana, donde cada minuto importa y el conocimiento adquiere verdadero valor cuando contribuye a salvar una vida.

INTELLIGENT CAD/CAM INTEGRATION FOR ADAPTIVE MANUFACTURING: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF AI AND IOT FRAMEWORKS IN INDUSTRY 4.0
abstractText: The union of Artificial Intelligence and the Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming the way Computer-Aided Design (CAD) and Computer-Aided Manufacturing (CAM) systems are used in the Industry 4.0 production process. Based on the PRISMA 2020 reporting framework (Page et al., 2021), this report is a systematic literature review on the intelligent integration of CAD and CAM technologies in adaptive manufacturing. Based on a structured search of major scientific databases, a curated list of peer-reviewed studies was analysed thematically to address five research questions related to designing with AI, toolpath optimisation using AI, IoT/IIoT architectures for real-time adaptive control, interoperability standards and barriers to AI adoption in specific sectors. AI models, especially deep learning, graph neural networks and reinforcement learning, have led the way in recent research and development on automatic feature recognition and toolpath generation, while digital twins, edge computing and Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) sensor networks are more and more being used to implement predictive maintenance and closed-loop adaptive control in the shop floor. The design phase is also starting to change with Generative AI to enable manufacturability constraints to be built in earlier in the CAD process. The literature, however, shows that there are still significant gaps that need to be addressed: AI models deployed outside of the simulation environment are not adaptable in real-time, training datasets are not standardized and openly shared, and there are interoperability protocols that are still quite disjointed, and resources for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) looking to use these technologies are still limited. To situate these gaps in a particular developing-economy context, this review is also supplemented by a series of recently published empirical studies. The review suggests that interoperability standards, Human Safety for Industry 5.0 design principles, cybersecurity, and sustainable practice are the key factors that need to be coordinated for the intelligent CAD/CAM-IoT integration to be fully realised, and it presents a roadmap of future research directions for adaptive and connected manufacturing ecosystems.

title: Sepsis en el Perú: de las guías internacionales a la adaptación local
abstractText: La sepsis es una emergencia tiempo-dependiente cuyo reconocimiento y tratamiento inicial ocurren principalmente en los servicios de emergencia. En el Perú y otros entornos con recursos limitados, las desigualdades en infraestructura, disponibilidad de personal, capacidad diagnóstica y acceso a cuidados críticos dificultan la aplicación uniforme de las guías internacionales. El abordaje inicial debe priorizar la identificación del deterioro clínico, la evaluación de la probabilidad de infección, el tratamiento antimicrobiano oportuno, la reanimación hemodinámica individualizada, el inicio de vasopresores cuando estén indicados y el control del foco infeccioso. Herramientas como NEWS2, MEWS, qSOFA y UVA pueden apoyar la detección y estratificación del riesgo, pero no sustituyen el juicio clínico ni deben utilizarse de manera aislada. La ausencia de registros regionales consolidados, las dificultades de referencia y la limitada disponibilidad de insumos restringen la implementación de protocolos estandarizados. El manejo de la sepsis en el Perú requiere adaptar la evidencia internacional a cada nivel de atención mediante protocolos pragmáticos, capacitación continua, indicadores de calidad, registros multicéntricos y redes eficientes de referencia. Esta adaptación debe preservar las intervenciones esenciales y evaluar su efectividad en la población peruana.

title: The Relationship between Overthinking and Academic Anxiety among Ninth-Grade Students at Madrasah Tsanawiyah Negeri 4 Kota Jambi
abstractText: Overthinking and academic anxiety are relevant psychological concerns during adolescence, yet their relationship among madrasah tsanawiyah students remains insufficiently examined. This study investigated the relationship between overthinking and academic anxiety among ninth-grade students at MTsN 4 Kota Jambi. A quantitative correlational design involved 122 students selected from a population of 175 through proportionate stratified random sampling. Data were collected using the Perseverative Thinking Questionnaire (PTQ) and an academic anxiety scale and analyzed using Pearson’s product–moment correlation. The results indicated a statistically significant positive correlation between overthinking and academic anxiety (r = .467, p < .001), corresponding to 21.8% shared variance. Students reporting higher levels of overthinking also tended to report greater academic anxiety. These findings provide contextual evidence of the association between repetitive negative thinking and academic anxiety within madrasah tsanawiyah education, highlighting the relevance of students’ cognitive patterns to their academic emotional experiences. The study suggests that school counselors should consider repetitive and unproductive thinking patterns when designing services to help students manage academic concerns more adaptively. Future research should include more diverse student populations and examine additional psychological and contextual factors associated with academic anxiety.

title: Strategi Guru Dalam Menstimulasi Kemampuan Mengenal Huruf Abjad Melalui Media Kartu Huruf Pada Anak Usia 4-5 Tahun
abstractText: Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi pentingnya stimulasi keaksaraan awal anak usia dini melalui kegiatan bermain yang bermakna dan menyenangkan, bukan pembelajaran calistung formal. Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan (1) strategi guru dalam menstimulasi kemampuan mengenal huruf abjad melalui media kartu huruf, (2) kemampuan mengenal huruf anak usia 4–5 tahun, dan (3) faktor pendukung dan penghambat di RA Al Husna Gersik Kediri. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan data yang dikumpulkan melalui observasi, wawancara, dan dokumentasi. Analisis data menggunakan model Miles, Huberman, dan Saldaña melalui kondensasi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan kesimpulan dan verifikasi. Keabsahan data diuji melalui triangulasi sumber dan teknik. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa: (1) guru menerapkan strategi demonstrasi, belajar sambil bermain melalui permainan “Berburu Kartu Huruf”, dan kelompok heterogen yang mendorong tutor sebaya; (2) media kartu huruf mendukung kemampuan keaksaraan awal, ditunjukkan oleh 12 dari 16 anak yang mampu menyebutkan huruf A–Z, membedakan huruf mirip, mengelompokkan huruf vokal dan konsonan, serta menyusun kata sederhana; dan (3) faktor pendukung meliputi media menarik, kreativitas guru, serta kerja sama orang tua, sedangkan hambatannya meliputi rentang atensi pendek, perilaku anak yang berubah-ubah, dan kurangnya pengulangan di rumah. Guru mengatasinya melalui pendekatan individual, variasi permainan, dan komunikasi dengan orang tua.

Emotion Regulation and Prosocial Behavior among Eleventh-Grade Students at SMA Negeri 1 Talamau, Indonesia
abstractText: Emotion regulation is widely assumed to support adolescents’ prosocial behavior, yet evidence from Indonesian senior high schools remains inconsistent, particularly in rural settings. This study described emotion regulation and prosocial behavior among eleventh-grade students at SMA Negeri 1 Talamau, West Pasaman, Indonesia, and examined the relationship between these variables. A quantitative correlational design involved 65 students selected from a population of 187 through proportionate random sampling. Data were collected using Likert-type emotion regulation and prosocial behavior scales comprising 37 items (α = .918) and 38 items (α = .937), respectively. Descriptive percentage analysis and Pearson product-moment correlation were conducted following normality and linearity testing. Most students exhibited high emotion regulation (61.54%), while nearly half demonstrated very high prosocial behavior (49.23%). No students were classified in the low or very low categories. The correlation was positive but very weak and statistically nonsignificant (r = .185, p = .141). These findings provide no evidence of a statistically significant linear association within this sample and caution against assuming that higher emotion regulation necessarily corresponds to greater prosocial behavior in this school context. The study contributes contextual evidence to research on adolescent socioemotional development and recommends combining emotion regulation training with peer-based prosocial programs in school counseling. Future research should involve larger samples and examine empathy and school climate alongside emotion regulation.

Protocolo Operativo de Empaquetamiento Térmico para el Manejo Prehospitalario de la Hipotermia Accidental en Áreas Remotas
abstractText: Las operaciones de búsqueda y rescate en áreas remotas y de montaña exponen permanentemente a rescatistas y víctimas al riesgo crítico de hipotermia accidental. El presente protocolo técnico-operativo estandariza el procedimiento de estabilización calórica in situ y empaque aplicado por el Grupo de Operaciones Policiales Especiales (GOPE) de Carabineros de Chile para preservar la temperatura corporal, disminuir la morbimortalidad y asegurar la estabilidad vital durante la evacuación prehospitalaria. El protocolo describe un sistema integrado multicapa que mitiga los cuatro mecanismos de pérdida calórica (conducción, convección, radiación y evaporación) mediante el uso secuencial de colchonetas aislantes, sacos de dormir, mantas aluminizadas y un pañal absorbente diseñado para prevenir que el empaque térmico se vea saturado por la diuresis por frío. Asimismo, incorpora el recalentamiento activo in situ mediante el posicionamiento de botellas con agua a alta temperatura en puntos vasculares clave y el uso de una cobertura impermeable con accesos clínicos selectivos. Al alinearse con las directrices internacionales del protocolo DOKEI de la Policía de Hokkaido, la Wilderness Medical Society (WMS) y el Joint Trauma System (JTS), este procedimiento demuestra que la estabilización térmica activa previa al traslado y la movilización en bloque horizontal son determinantes para mitigar la irritabilidad miocárdica y el colapso cardiocirculatorio en áreas remotas.

Robust trajectory tracking of an underactuated ROV under compound flow disturbances using ADRC-GISMC
abstractText: Abstract Trajectory tracking of remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) remains difficult when hydrodynamic coupling, plant uncertainty, actuator constraints, and spatially varying flow disturbances act simultaneously. This study presents a simulation-based evaluation of an ADRC-GISMC strategy for an underactuated ROV under an engineering-oriented compound disturbance model combining background-current and local outfall-plume components. SMC, ADRC, ADRC-SMC, and ADRC-GISMC are compared using the same full six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body plant, rank-deficient thruster-allocation layer, reference trajectory, and actuator settings. Under the tested balanced and strong conditions, ADRC-GISMC does not minimize every tracking metric; instead, it provides a metric-dependent trade-off among position tracking, attitude response, executed moment-energy demand, and allocation feasibility. This trade-off is further examined through a paired Monte Carlo analysis with 100 plant-parameter samples, actuator-constraint and measurement/sampling tests, a local one-factor-at-a-time disturbance-sensitivity analysis, a local point-of-action sensitivity study, and geometric path-following and tolerance-band diagnostics. The results support ESO-based disturbance compensation combined with global integral sliding mode as an application-level control integration for the numerical evaluation of underactuated ROV trajectory tracking under the specified conditions. Accordingly, the conclusions are restricted to the specified numerical scenarios, parameter ranges, actuator settings, and evaluation metrics.

Effect Of the Edutainment Learning Model Assisted by Monopoly Game Media on The Learning Outcomes of Grade V Students in Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) at SDn 067246 Medan Tuntungan, Academic Year 2026/2027
abstractText: This study was motivated by the low learning outcomes of fifth-grade students in the Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) subject at SDN 067246 Medan Tuntungan. This condition was reflected in the lack of students’ attention and participation during the learning process, as well as the monotonous classroom atmosphere. The study aimed to determine the effect of the Edutainment learning model assisted by Monopoly game media on students’ learning outcomes in the IPAS topic “Indonesia Kaya Raya” among fifth-grade students at SDN 067246 Medan Tuntungan in the 2026/2027 Academic Year. This research employed a quantitative approach using a pre-experimental method with a One Group Pretest-Posttest Design. The sample consisted of 25 fifth-grade students. Data were collected through tests, observations, questionnaires, and documentation. Data analysis was conducted using descriptive statistics, normality testing, correlation analysis, coefficient of determination analysis, and hypothesis testing. The results showed that the average pretest score was 50.88, while the average posttest score increased to 84.80. The correlation test yielded a coefficient of 0.951, indicating a very strong relationship, while the coefficient of determination was 90.44%. The hypothesis test produced a significance value of 0.000 < 0.05, resulting in the rejection of H₀ and acceptance of Hₐ. Therefore, it can be concluded that the Edutainment learning model assisted by Monopoly game media had a significant effect on the learning outcomes of fifth-grade students in IPAS at SDN 067246 Medan Tuntungan in the 2026/2027 Academic Year.

title: Agility and Flexibility Strategies in Manufacturing Systems: A Systematic Review with a Focus on Sub-Saharan Africa
abstractText: Special companies, those in markets with fluctuating demand and supply, need to take the ups and downs in the market, disruption in their supply chains, and the technology and competitive pressure, and still maintain delivery, quality, and cost targets. The present systematic review, following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, aims at gathering 42 studies related to the manufacturing agility and flexibility, focusing on Sub Saharan Africa (SSA). The corpus consists of manufacturing flexibility, agile and leagile manufacturing, lean practice, supply-chain agility, digital transformation and Industry 4.0 and is segmented based on application domain, geography, methodology and publication period. The evidence suggests that agility and flexibility are associated with improved operational and organisational performance in SSA, but the pathways and degree of application varies significantly between firms and countries. The consistent challenges are cost, skills, infrastructure (reliability of power supply) and supply chain; management commitment is always cited as the final key. Digital technologies and Industry 4.0 are enablers that require a combination of infrastructure, organisational integration and human capability, and not just ownership of digital technology. There is some fragmentation in measurement of agility – different constructs are used in various surveys, there are formal agility indices, and new AI-assisted assessment frameworks are emerging – none of which have yet been validated for SSA. A series of shop-floor studies in Zimbabwe (process-parameter optimisation, data-driven maintenance, and agent-based condition monitoring) demonstrates that new capabilities at the operational level can be realized at relatively low costs, but are rarely related to the strategic agility literature. The conceptual framework and research agenda of the review call for a SSA-specific measurement tool, an integrated socio-technical model, operational as well as longitudinal evidence, and more robust mechanisms of building industry–academy capabilities, e.g., learning factories.

abstractText: В статье теоретически и эмпирически исследована роль механизмов стратегического управления в повышении конкурентоспособности коммерческих банков на примере банковской системы Узбекистана. Систематизированы научные подходы, основанные на теории конкурентного преимущества, ресурсной концепции, системе сбалансированных показателей, а также исследования банковской конкуренции и структуры собственности; предложена концептуальная модель влияния стратегического управления на конкурентоспособность банка. На основе данных Центрального банка Республики Узбекистан, Центра экономических исследований и реформ, Всемирного банка и Международного валютного фонда проведён сравнительный и графический анализ структуры собственности, рыночной концентрации, рентабельности, структуры фондирования и показателей цифровизации банковской системы. Результаты показывают, что доля банков с государственным участием в активах снизилась с 84 процентов в 2019 году до 62 процентов на 1 августа 2026 года, а активы частных банков росли быстрее (29 процентов против 14 процентов). Вместе с тем около 85 процентов прироста чистого дохода обеспечено непроцентными доходами, а соотношение кредитов и депозитов в банках с государственным участием составляет 170 процентов. Для коммерческих банков Узбекистана разработана семиэтапная модель совершенствования механизма стратегического управления.

Effect of Aloe barbadensis gel on hematology, mortality rate and behavioral attributes of broiler chickens
abstractText: The study evaluated the effects of dietary supplementation of Aloe barbadensis M. (also known as Aloe vera) gel on the hematological, biochemical, and behavioral responses of broiler chickens fed at four dietary levels (T1-T4). Among the hematological indices assessed, Mean Corpuscular Haemoglobin (MCH) was the only parameter significantly affected by treatment, with T4 recording the highest value (35.3 mm/hr) and T3 the lowest (30.3 mm/hr); Duncan's Multiple Range Test (DMRT) separated the means in the order T4 > T1 > T2 > T3, with T3 significantly lower than T4. All other hematological indices, such as PCV, Hb, WBC, RBC, MCV, MCHC, and the neutrophil, lymphocyte, and monocyte differential counts did not significantly differ among the treatments. Whereas serum conjugated bilirubin was the only highly significant parameter in the serum biochemical assessment, with T1 recording the highest value (1.100 µmol/L), significantly greater than T2, T3, and T4, which did not differ from one another. Electrolytes, kidney function markers (urea, creatinine), liver enzymes (ASAT, ALAT, ALP), total bilirubin, total protein, and albumin were unaffected by treatment, and all kidney and liver markers remained within normal physiological ranges across treatments. None of the eight behavioral variables assessed differed significantly among treatments, although Feeding and Drinking behaviors showed numerical trends approaching significance. These findings suggest that Aloe barbadensis gel supplementation had a largely neutral effect on the overall hematological, biochemical, and behavioral status of broiler chickens, with isolated effects on MCH and conjugated bilirubin that do not indicate hepatotoxic or nephrotoxic outcomes.

title: Landscape composition and photoperiod shape differences in space use and hunting behaviour between boreal and Alpine pygmy owl populations
abstractText: Abstract Context Investigating how habitat specialists express population-level differences in habitat preferences and movement behaviour across contrasting landscapes and abiotic environments allows us to distinguish patterns that are consistent across populations from those that are population-specific responses to local conditions. Objectives We examined space use, hunting habitat selection and diel activity between Eurasian Pygmy Owl ( Glaucidium passerinum ) populations occupying boreal (south-west Finland) and subalpine (Western Italian Alps) forests, to assess the consistency of these patterns across regions with contrasting landscape structure and photoperiod. Methods From 2021 to 2024, we GPS-tagged 26 breeding males (13 per region), obtaining 6076 GPS locations. We estimated 90% home-range areas using autocorrelated kernel density estimators (AKDE). Hunting habitat selection was examined with resource selection functions implemented as GLMMs, and diel activity was characterised by modelling activity probability with cyclic GAMs. Results Pygmy owls behaved as clear forest specialists in both regions: 90% AKDE home ranges were dominated by continuous forest, with consistent avoidance of open habitats and recent clear-cuts. Activity was diurnal, with peaks at dawn and dusk. Boreal individuals showed extended activity periods associated with prolonged daylight and twilight. Home ranges were approximately twice as large in boreal forests, and daily movement distances were about one third greater, indicating context-dependent behavioural responses. Conclusions Population-level differences in space use and activity of pygmy owls were consistent with contrasting landscape and photoperiodic conditions, whereas strong reliance on mature forest was consistent across regions. This dependence may constrain responses of forest specialists to rapid habitat change, emphasising the need to maintain structurally complex forest landscapes.
